newsitem.title: USA: Fran downgraded to depression, rains still heavy.
newsitem.headline: Fran downgraded to depression, rains still heavy.

text.p: Tropical storm warnings for the southeastern United States were discontinued Friday afternoon as the remains of Hurricane Fran moved inland and the storm continued to weaken, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 1400 EDT/1800 GMT, Fran was downgraded to a tropical depression. Its center was near latitude 37.9 north and longitude 79.4 west, or about 30 miles (48 km) east of Hot Springs, Virginia, and moving north-northwest near 15 mph (24 kmh). Forecasters said a gradual turn to the north, more weakening, and deceleration was expected during the next 24 hours.
Maximum sustained winds had decreased to 35 mph (56 kmh) with higher gusts mainly over the coastal waters of Virginia and the Chesapeake Bay.
Forecasters warned of more flooding, saying six to eight inches (15-13 cm) of rainfall was possible over parts of Virginia, Maryland, West Virginia and Pennsylvania along Fran's path.
